label: def:horizon-functor
title: Horizon functor
html:
Definition. Horizon functor

Let \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) denote the observable subcategory . Let \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}) denote its set of connected components (the aeons, aeon).

The horizon functor is the map

  \partial \colon 
  \pi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V))\bigr)
  \longrightarrow 
  \mathcal{P}\!\bigl(
    \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V))
    \setminus
    \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V))
  \bigr).

It sends each aeon \mathcal{A} to its boundary. This boundary comprises configurations \mathcal{S} that appear as limits of diagrams in \mathcal{A} but have A_0|_{\mathcal{S}} = 0:

  \partial(\mathcal{A})
  = 
  \bigl\{
    \mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{Bun} \setminus \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}
    : 
    \mathcal{S} = \varinjlim D
    \text{ for some directed diagram } D \subset \mathcal{A}
  \bigr\}.

Every element of \partial(\mathcal{A}) defines a jet horizon .

Functoriality. If \mathcal{A} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{A}' is an inclusion of connected components, then \mathcal{A} = \mathcal{A}' by maximality, and \partial acts as the identity. For adjacent aeons \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{A}' , the intersection \partial(\mathcal{A}) \cap \partial(\mathcal{A}') \neq \varnothing. These shared boundary objects specify the loci where the CCC transition occurs.

Relation to the torsion flow. The torsion flow \Phi_t^q provides an endofunctor of \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)). Within an aeon, \Phi_t^q restricts to an endofunctor of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} (preserving A_0 \neq 0). The horizon \partial(\mathcal{A}) constitutes the set of fixed points of the limiting behaviour \Phi_t^q \to \partial as t approaches the aeon boundary.
